record_body:
Account summary (ABM Healthcare vertical)
- Helios Labs = B2B healthtech platform (care coordination + clinician workflow tooling). Handles PHI; sells into provider groups + some payer programs.
- Current state: mix of vendor LLM APIs + limited internal GPU for smaller models; key complaint is unpredictable latency + cost when usage spikes.
- Interest: Redwood Private in their VPC to keep PHI controls + simplify security review with hospital partners. Dedicated is fallback if Private timeline is long.

Primary contacts (as captured)
- Maya R. (Security & Compliance lead) — driving questionnaire + PHI boundaries
- Dan H. (Director, Platform Engineering) — owns VPC/network, logging/SIEM, SSO
- Priya S. (Applied ML lead) — owns eval harness + model quality; interested in caching/batching mechanics and regression monitoring

Use cases / workload notes
- Clinical note summarization (async + some near-real-time): long-ish inputs (2k–8k tokens), output 200–600 tokens.
- Provider inbox triage (interactive): shorter prompts but stricter latency.
- Patient chart Q&A / doc search: embeddings + reranking; wants consistent throughput for batch ingestion.

Technical deep dive notes (batching / caching)
- They asked explicitly: “If we use streaming, does batching still help?”
  - SE note: explain continuous batching: even with streaming, runtime can batch prefill/attention steps across concurrent requests; token-by-token decode batching depends on arrival patterns.
- Latency SLO targets (their stated goals)
  - Interactive triage: p95 TTFT < 800ms in-region; p95 end-to-end < 6s for typical responses.
  - Summarization: p95 < 20s acceptable for longer notes (async acceptable).
- Concurrency expectations
  - Peak hours (clinic): 150–250 concurrent in interactive endpoints; summarization bursts after uploads.
- Caching questions
  - Prefix caching: they have stable system prompt + policy boilerplate; wants to reuse across requests.
  - KV cache reuse: asked about “session reuse for follow-up questions” (chart Q&A). Action: map to Redwood cache semantics + routing policy.
- Redwood levers they cared about
  - Ability to set max batch size / latency ceiling (“don’t batch at the expense of interactive UX”).
  - Visibility in Console: token-level cost, queueing vs compute time, batch efficiency over time.
  - Quality guardrails if we suggest quantization: “we can’t regress hallucination rate in clinical summaries.”

Data residency + PHI handling
- Residency requirement: US-only processing for PHI (today). They have a subset of non-PHI analytics that can be processed globally but prefer to keep everything US to simplify audits.
- They asked: “Do you store prompts/outputs by default?”
  - Logged answer (approved language): Redwood can operate with restricted retention; log/audit controls configurable; details to be confirmed in writing via security FAQ + NDA materials. Avoid over-promising.
- They want audit logs exported to their SIEM (Splunk) with consistent event schema.

Decision criteria for Private deployment (what they said they’ll evaluate)
1) Security/compliance posture
   - SOC 2 evidence + questionnaire responsiveness
   - SSO/SAML + RBAC model
   - Audit logging: admin actions, model/version changes, access to inference endpoints; export to Splunk
   - Encryption: in-transit + at-rest; KMS integration for customer-managed keys (preferred)
   - Retention controls for logs/prompts/outputs + ability to document PHI boundaries
2) Network and deployment architecture
   - Private connectivity: VPC peering / PrivateLink-style patterns acceptable
   - No public internet path required for inference traffic (strong preference)
   - Clear shared responsibility model (Redwood vs Helios)
3) Performance + predictability
   - Can we meet TTFT + p95 under peak concurrency with batching/caching tuned?
   - Can we reserve capacity / avoid noisy neighbor effects (this is why Private > Hosted)
4) Operability
   - Upgrade/rollout model for Private (how are model versions pinned? rollback?)
   - Observability hooks: metrics + tracing integration; ability to correlate latency spikes with batch settings

Activity timeline (recent)
- 2026-01-23: Inbound via Healthcare regulated workloads landing page (UTM: abm_healthcare_private). Diego qualified; routed to Colin for technical scoping.
- 2026-01-30: Discovery call (Diego + Colin): confirmed PHI, US residency, strong VPC requirement; Dedicated as plan B.
- 2026-02-14: Technical deep dive (platform + ML): focused on batching, caching, performance sizing; requested written notes + architecture diagram.
- 2026-02-19: Security follow-up (Maya R.): asked for retention/residency statement and audit log export details; requested evidence list under NDA.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Confirm whether any data must be processed on-prem (they said: potential future hospital partner requirement; not immediate).
- Need sample traffic patterns (arrival rate distribution) to size batching policies and capacity.
- Identify model shortlist (they currently use a mix; want Redwood recommendation but will run their eval harness).

Internal notes (deal strategy)
- Lead with Private/VPC story + auditability + predictable unit economics; don’t get pulled into “we’re a generic model API.”
- Offer: 2–3 week structured eval in their VPC with defined SLOs + cost targets; use Console dashboards as proof.
- If Private procurement drags, propose Dedicated as interim with explicit path to Private (avoid 'bait and switch').

Next steps (owner)
- Diego: send recap + propose dates for architecture review w/ Dan H. + Maya R.; include links to Healthcare Security FAQ addendum + reference architecture.
- Colin: draft a proposed batching/caching configuration hypothesis for their two endpoint types (interactive vs async) + list what traffic samples we need.
- Security (Olga/Marcus): provide questionnaire evidence checklist + confirm shareable artifacts under NDA.
